title: Evaluate raising bronze_ingest_wgi per_page — measured, rejected, reverted
description: Every World Bank API request is an independent chance to hit the intermittent read timeout that stopped bronze_WGI completing on 2026-08-03, so raising per_page (1000 -> 10000, cutting ~36 requests per run to ~6) looked like the highest-leverage reliability change available. It was shipped, measured against the live API the same day, and REJECTED: the request-count saving is swamped by per-request cost, and the change makes the notebook more fragile rather than less. Reverted to per_page=1000. The deliverable is the measurement and the DO-NOT-RAISE note in the notebook, not the change.
acceptanceCriteria: per_page is a named module-level constant (API_PAGE_SIZE) rather than an inline literal, matching the constant style task-050 established.
The raised value is measured against the live API rather than reasoned about — request count, per-request latency, fetch-cell duration and record counts all recorded.
Data equivalence is checked explicitly, so a latency finding is never confused with a correctness one.
The measured outcome is acted on whatever it says, including reverting the change if it is worse — a negative result is a valid outcome, not a failed task.
The finding is recorded where the next person to have this idea will read it (the notebook's own constant block), not only in task notes.
If reverted, the task-012_1 baseline comparability is restored and task-012_5's notes and performance_optimized.md are corrected accordingly.
notes: CREATED 2026-08-03 (/work, Erik-approved). Splits out the change task-050 note 3 explicitly deferred ('DELIBERATELY NOT DOING: raising per_page ... Revisit AFTER task-012_5 closes'). Erik chose to take it early rather than wait out the API degradation.
SHIPPED THEN REVERTED 2026-08-03, same day. Commit e785d4c raised API_PAGE_SIZE to 10000; the revert follows in the next commit. Both are Erik-approved decisions taken with the measurement in hand.

MEASUREMENT (live standalone run, 2026-08-03 18:46, per_page=10000). Fetch cell 8m16s (496s) vs 265s for the per_page=1000 run earlier the same day — roughly TWICE AS SLOW. One timeout logged (VA.EST page 1, 4.9s backoff, ~125s cost), leaving ~371s across 7 successful requests = ~53s per request. The 265s run's timeouts were inferred from arithmetic rather than a log, so per-request cost there is bounded at 0.4s (2 timeouts) to 3.9s (1 timeout); 3 timeouts is arithmetically impossible. Per-request cost therefore rose between 13x and 130x — the conclusion holds across the whole uncertainty range.

WHY IT BACKFIRED — two independent reasons, both now in the notebook's constant block: (1) SLOWER — the World Bank API charges far more to serialise one ~5,150-record page than six 1,000-record pages, which swamps the 36->6 request saving. (2) MORE FRAGILE — at ~53s against a 120s read timeout every request sits at ~44% of its budget, versus under 3% at per_page=1000. Large pages move every request toward the ceiling instead of reducing exposure, which is exactly how VA.EST page 1 timed out during the run intended to demonstrate the improvement. The premise 'fewer requests = fewer chances to fail' ignores that per-request failure probability is not independent of page size.

DATA EQUIVALENCE CONFIRMED, so this is purely a latency/robustness finding and not a correctness one: 31,122 records total at per_page=10000, with CC.EST 5158 / GE.EST 5127 / PV.EST 5214 matching the earlier per_page=1000 partial run EXACTLY on all three indicators it had reached. Pagination is driven by the API's own metadata 'pages' value, so neither value truncates.

BASELINE RESTORED: the re-baselining cost recorded against task-012_5 is withdrawn. per_page is back to 1000, so the task-012_1 bronze_WGI figure (73s) is a like-for-like comparison again and task-012_5 can report a real bronze delta. task-012_5 notes and performance_optimized.md corrected in the same commit.

STANDING CONCLUSION: task-050's capped exponential backoff is what actually fixed the degraded-API case — the 265s run completed where the notebook had failed twice that morning. per_page was a fix for a problem task-050 had already solved.
